biography.plain_text: Tim Steiner is a British entrepreneur who co-founded Ocado after eight years trading bonds at Goldman Sachs. He established the online grocer with Jonathan Faiman and Jason Gissing, retaining a substantial shareholding as chief executive. The company developed its own systems and expanded into supplying automated fulfilment technology to other retailers.

long_biography.plain_text:
Ocado co-founder Tim Steiner learned warehouse engineering while trying to make the company’s first distribution centre work. Faced with conveyor bottlenecks, he took a laptop home and redesigned the rules governing how goods moved through the building. Software specialists implemented the changes; weekly orders rose from six thousand to ten thousand within weeks.

His approach to development included allowing teams to experiment and accept unsuccessful trials. Ocado also built a shared software platform for its retail partners: a feature requested in one market could become available to all. Comparing performance across their warehouses helped identify where individual operations could improve.
